Use it as the at-a-glance pulse before reading the deeper panels, noting the new PPWR PFAS limits.

c-freight.simple: These are the speedometers of shipping — bulk (BDI) and container (FEU) show how fast freight costs move.
expert: FRED's deep-sea PPI and Cass index are official, free monthly readings of freight cost and volume.
BDI signals bulk/dry demand; container FEU rates drive your boxed-goods landed cost.
Monthly series lag 1–2 months — use the official source links for the latest spot figures, noting mixed Transpacific and Asia-Europe trends.

c-curve.simple: Like a tide chart — it tells you if prices are heading up (lock now) or down (wait).
expert: A rising curve (contango) means forward prices are higher, so locking now can pay off.
A falling curve (backwardation) means the market expects easing — less urgency.
Steel, oil, resin and freight each give their own procurement-timing signal, with Brent easing to $98.00/bbl.

c-cost.simple: Shows what really fills your cost pie — raw material is just one slice, not the whole pie.
expert: Raw materials are a minority of landed cost; conversion, freight and duty dominate — so a dip in one index moves your price far less than the headline.
That's why Birdland's quotes reflect secured materials and reliable supply, not yesterday's spot price.
Hover a segment to see each component's share, considering the impact of new PPWR PFAS limits on packaging.

c-duty.simple: A toll calculator for imports — pick the country and the origin, and it shows the import tax on your route.
expert: Switching origin (Taiwan vs China) shows how much tariff stacking you avoid.
Figures are illustrative for garden hand-tools — confirm your HS code with your broker.
Pair it with the cost breakdown to see duty's real weight, especially with new US tariff measures in effect and Canada's increased surtaxes on US-origin steel.

c-mkt.simple: Like reading two top weather stations (BNP Paribas & Citi), then telling you what to pack for your market.
expert: Cross-referencing publicly reported BNP Paribas and Citi research: Citi now anticipates Brent crude volatility due to the severe disruption of the Strait of Hormuz, with prices easing to $98.00/bbl on October 1, 2026, despite US mine-clearing efforts and Iran-Oman talks for a temporary corridor, before potentially easing later in 2026, impacting fuel- and freight-linked costs.

BNP Paribas flags tariff-reconfiguration risk (the US tariff court ruling, USMCA renegotiation), new Canada surtaxes on US-origin steel, and China–EU trade tensions as key watch-items, alongside ongoing Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz disruptions.

Birdland's takeaway for your sourcing: prioritize locking supply and keeping origin flexible to navigate tariff rules and geopolitical risks, treating current price fluctuations as a call for stability.

advice.zh: 【Birdland 供應鏈週報】本週亞洲—美西運價混合走勢 (洛杉磯穩定在 $7,835/FEU, 紐約漲 1% 至 $10,428/FEU), 亞洲—歐洲海運運價回軟 (鹿特丹跌 2% 至 $3,399/FEU, 熱那亞跌 3% 至 $3,702/FEU)。 北美鋼價受關稅支撐穩定,全球趨勢分歧,中國鋼廠減產護價; 木材與塑膠粒則持續走軟。 Brent原油因荷姆茲海峽局勢高度不穩，伊朗持續針對商業航運而回落至 $98.00 美元/桶。 建議:海運運價混合走勢,應戰略性訂艙,並分批鎖定鋼質料件與燃料相關投入。美方新關稅措施已生效,加拿大對美國鋼鋁產品加徵關稅至50%,請留意。 法規面 EUDR(2026/12/30)木柄文件請務必提早備齊,並留意PPWR(2026/8/12)對包裝PFAS的限制,該限制已生效。 需要我們協助規劃備料節奏與文件,隨時聯繫。
advice.en: [Birdland Supply-Chain Brief] Transpacific ocean freight rates are mixed, with Shanghai to Los Angeles stable at $7,835/FEU and Shanghai to New York up 1% to $10,428/FEU. Asia–Europe rates are softening, with Rotterdam down 2% to $3,399/FEU and Genoa down 3% to $3,702/FEU. North American steel prices are stable, supported by tariffs, while global trends are mixed with China mills cutting production to defend prices; lumber and resin continue to soften. Brent crude eased to $98.00 USD/bbl on October 1, 2026, as the Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted with Iran continuing to target commercial shipping. We suggest strategically booking ocean space given the mixed freight trends, and phasing in steel-input and fuel-linked cover. New US tariff measures are now in effect, and Canada has increased surtaxes on US-origin steel and aluminum to 50% from September 8, 2026, requiring close monitoring. On compliance, prepare EUDR (30 Dec 2026) timber documentation early and thoroughly, and note PPWR (12 Aug 2026) PFAS limits for packaging, which are now in effect. Contact us to plan your buying cadence and paperwork.
